source.text: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מְגוּרֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt Jacob in [the] land of [the] sojournings of his father, in [the] land of Canaan.

en.L: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.
en.B: Jacob stayed on in the land where his father had lived as a foreigner, the land of Canaan.
en.R: Jacob lived in Canaan, the land where his father Isaac had lived as a foreigner.

es.L: Y habitó Jacob en la tierra de las peregrinaciones de su padre, en la tierra de Canaán.
es.B: Jacob se quedó a vivir en la tierra donde su padre había residido como extranjero, la tierra de Canaán.
es.R: Jacob vivió en Canaán, la tierra donde su padre Isaac había vivido como extranjero.

fr.L: Et Jacob habita dans le pays des séjours de son père, au pays de Canaan.
fr.B: Jacob demeura dans le pays où son père avait vécu en étranger, le pays de Canaan.
fr.R: Jacob a vécu dans le pays de Canaan, là où son père Isaac avait vécu comme un étranger.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akakaa katika nchi ya ugeni wa baba yake, katika nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.B: Yakobo aliendelea kuishi katika nchi ambayo baba yake alikuwa ameishi kama mgeni, yaani nchi ya Kanaani.
sw.R: Yakobo aliishi Kanaani, nchi ambayo baba yake Isaka aliishi kama mgeni.

decisions.choice: his father's sojournings: where Isaac lived as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The word means living in a land as an outsider without owning it. Esau has just settled in Seir (36:8); Jacob stays in the promised land, still as a guest in it, as Abraham and Isaac were (17:8; Hebrews 11:9).

decisions.choice: his father Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable names the father for clarity.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("habita", "demeura"); passé composé at Readable ("a vécu"); speech in the passé composé at every level, including the retelling of the dreams
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative, the passé composé the tense of spoken French and of the plain Readable level. Joseph's telling of his dreams (verses 7, 9) is speech, so it stays in the tenses of speech.

source.text: אֵ֣לֶּה׀תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־דִּבָּתָ֥ם רָעָ֖ה אֶל־אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] generations of Jacob. Joseph, a son of seventeen year[s], was shepherding with his brothers in the flock; and he [was] a youth with [the] sons of Bilhah and with [the] sons of Zilpah, [the] wives of his father; and brought Joseph their report, bad, to their father.

en.L: These [are] the generations of Jacob. Joseph, [being] seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers. He [was] a young man with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.
en.B: This is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was seventeen, he used to tend the flocks with his brothers, working as a helper alongside the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, two of his father's wives. Joseph brought their father an unfavorable report about them.
en.R: Here is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he took care of the sheep and goats with his brothers. He worked with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, who were wives of his father. Joseph told his father bad things about what his brothers were doing.

es.L: Estas [son] las generaciones de Jacob. José, de diecisiete años, pastoreaba el rebaño con sus hermanos. Él [era] un muchacho con los hijos de Bilhá y con los hijos de Zilpá, mujeres de su padre. Y José llevó a su padre malos informes de ellos.
es.B: Esta es la historia de la familia de Jacob. Cuando José tenía diecisiete años, cuidaba los rebaños con sus hermanos, como ayudante de los hijos de Bilhá y de Zilpá, dos de las mujeres de su padre. José le llevó a su padre un mal informe acerca de ellos.
es.R: Esta es la historia de la familia de Jacob. Cuando José tenía diecisiete años, cuidaba las ovejas y las cabras con sus hermanos. Trabajaba con los hijos de Bilhá y de Zilpá, que eran mujeres de su padre. José le contó a su padre las cosas malas que hacían sus hermanos.

fr.L: Voici les générations de Jacob. Joseph, [âgé] de dix-sept ans, faisait paître le troupeau avec ses frères. Il [était] un jeune garçon avec les fils de Bilha et avec les fils de Zilpa, femmes de son père. Et Joseph rapporta à leur père de mauvais propos sur eux.
fr.B: Voici l’histoire de la famille de Jacob. À dix-sept ans, Joseph gardait les troupeaux avec ses frères ; il servait d’aide aux fils de Bilha et de Zilpa, deux des femmes de son père. Et Joseph fit à leur père un rapport défavorable sur eux.
fr.R: Voici l’histoire de la famille de Jacob. Quand Joseph avait dix-sept ans, il s’occupait des moutons et des chèvres avec ses frères. Il travaillait avec les fils de Bilha et de Zilpa, qui étaient des femmes de son père. Joseph a raconté à son père les mauvaises choses que faisaient ses frères.

sw.L: Hivi ni vizazi vya Yakobo. Yusufu, [akiwa] mwenye umri wa miaka kumi na saba, alikuwa akichunga kundi pamoja na ndugu zake. Naye [alikuwa] kijana pamoja na wana wa Bilha na wana wa Zilpa, wake za baba yake. Naye Yusufu akamletea baba yao habari mbaya juu yao.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo habari ya jamaa ya Yakobo. Yusufu alipokuwa na umri wa miaka kumi na saba, alikuwa akichunga makundi pamoja na ndugu zake, akiwasaidia wana wa Bilha na wa Zilpa, wawili kati ya wake za baba yake. Yusufu akampelekea baba yao habari zisizo njema kuwahusu.
sw.R: Hii ni habari ya jamaa ya Yakobo. Yusufu alipokuwa na miaka kumi na saba, alichunga kondoo na mbuzi pamoja na ndugu zake. Alifanya kazi pamoja na wana wa Bilha na Zilpa, waliokuwa wake za baba yake. Yusufu alimweleza baba yake mambo mabaya ambayo ndugu zake walikuwa wakifanya.

decisions.choice: the generations of Jacob: the heading of the story of Jacob's sons
decisions.reason: This heading (toledot) opens each major section of Genesis (2:4; 6:9; 11:27; 25:19). What follows is less a list of names than the story of Jacob's family, centered on Joseph and Judah, to the end of the book.

decisions.choice: a youth with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah: a junior helper
decisions.reason: Na'ar means a young man, and often a young helper or attendant. Joseph works under the sons of the two slave wives.

decisions.choice: a bad report of them: an unfavorable account, perhaps slander
decisions.reason: The phrase (dibbah ra'ah) can mean an accurate but damaging report or a malicious one (Numbers 13:32). The narrator does not say whether Joseph's report was true.

source.text: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִכָּל־בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי־בֶן־זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ כְּתֹ֥נֶת פַּסִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, for a son of old age [was] he to him; and he made for him a tunic of palms.

en.L: And Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he [was] the son of his old age; and he made him a tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles].
en.B: Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, since he had been born to him in his old age, and he had a long-sleeved robe made for him.
en.R: Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because Joseph was born when Israel was old. Israel gave Joseph a special robe with long sleeves.

es.L: E Israel amaba a José más que a todos sus hijos, porque [era] el hijo de su vejez; y le hizo una túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos].
es.B: Israel quería a José más que a ninguno de sus otros hijos, porque le había nacido en su vejez, y le mandó hacer una túnica larga con mangas.
es.R: Israel amaba a José más que a todos sus otros hijos, porque José nació cuando Israel ya era viejo. Israel le regaló a José una túnica especial de mangas largas.

fr.L: Et Israël aimait Joseph plus que tous ses fils, car il [était] pour lui le fils de [sa] vieillesse ; et il lui fit une tunique [qui descendait jusqu’aux] poignets [et aux chevilles].
fr.B: Israël aimait Joseph plus que tous ses autres fils, parce qu’il lui était né dans sa vieillesse, et il lui fit faire une longue tunique à manches.
fr.R: Israël aimait Joseph plus que tous ses autres fils, parce que Joseph était né quand Israël était déjà vieux. Israël a donné à Joseph une belle tunique avec de longues manches.

sw.L: Naye Israeli alimpenda Yusufu kuliko wana wake wote, kwa kuwa [alikuwa] mwana wa uzee wake; naye akamfanyia kanzu [iliyofika hadi] vifundo [vya mikono na miguu].
sw.B: Israeli alimpenda Yusufu kuliko wana wake wengine wote, kwa kuwa alikuwa amempata katika uzee wake, naye akamshonea kanzu ndefu yenye mikono mirefu.
sw.R: Israeli alimpenda Yusufu kuliko wana wake wengine wote, kwa sababu Yusufu alizaliwa Israeli alipokuwa mzee. Israeli alimpa Yusufu kanzu ya pekee yenye mikono mirefu.

decisions.choice: a tunic of passim: a long robe reaching to the wrists and ankles
decisions.reason: Passim probably means "palms (of the hands) and soles (of the feet)": a full-length robe with long sleeves, not the short working tunic of a shepherd. The ancient Greek translation took it as "many-colored", the source of the familiar "coat of many colors". The only other such garment in Scripture is worn by a king's daughter (2 Samuel 13:18-19). Either way it marked Joseph out as favored and exempt from hard work.

decisions.choice: the son of his old age: born late in Jacob's life
decisions.reason: Joseph was the first son of Rachel, Jacob's loved wife, born after long waiting (30:22-24). Benjamin is younger, but Joseph is the son of Jacob's old age in the story's eyes.

decisions.choice: a long-sleeved robe
decisions.reason: The familiar rendering follows the Greek translation; the Hebrew points to the robe's length and sleeves rather than its color.

decisions.choice: "kanzu" for the tunic (ketonet) at every level, in verses 3, 23, 31-33
decisions.reason: A "kanzu" is the long, full-length robe with sleeves that East African men wear, which is just what the meaning decision describes (reaching to wrists and ankles). "Joho" is an open overcoat or academic gown, and "vazi" is any garment.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי־אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכָּל־אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּשְׂנְא֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ דַּבְּר֥וֹ לְשָׁלֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw his brothers that him loved their father more than all his brothers, and they hated him and were not able to speak to him for peace.

en.L: And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him and could not speak to him peaceably.
en.B: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, and they hated him so much that they could not say a friendly word to him.
en.R: His brothers could see that their father loved Joseph more than any of them. So they hated Joseph and could not even speak kindly to him.

es.L: Y vieron sus hermanos que su padre lo amaba más que a todos sus hermanos, y lo odiaron y no podían hablarle en paz.
es.B: Sus hermanos vieron que su padre lo quería más que a todos ellos, y lo odiaban tanto que no eran capaces de dirigirle una palabra amable.
es.R: Sus hermanos se dieron cuenta de que su padre quería a José más que a todos ellos. Por eso odiaban a José y ni siquiera podían hablarle con amabilidad.

fr.L: Et ses frères virent que leur père l’aimait plus que tous ses frères, et ils le haïrent, et ils ne pouvaient pas lui parler en paix.
fr.B: Ses frères virent que leur père l’aimait plus qu’eux tous, et ils le prirent en haine, au point qu’ils ne pouvaient plus lui adresser une parole aimable.
fr.R: Ses frères ont bien vu que leur père aimait Joseph plus qu’eux tous. Alors ils ont détesté Joseph, et ils ne pouvaient même pas lui parler gentiment.

sw.L: Nao ndugu zake wakaona kwamba baba yao alimpenda kuliko ndugu zake wote, wakamchukia, wala hawakuweza kuzungumza naye kwa amani.
sw.B: Ndugu zake walipoona kwamba baba yao alimpenda kuliko wao wote, walimchukia kiasi kwamba hawakuweza kumwambia neno lolote la kirafiki.
sw.R: Ndugu zake waliona kwamba baba yao alimpenda Yusufu kuliko wao wote. Kwa hiyo walimchukia Yusufu, na hawakuweza hata kuongea naye kwa upole.

decisions.choice: speak to him for peace: speak to him in a friendly way
decisions.reason: To speak "for peace" (shalom) is to speak on good terms, and may include the ordinary greeting. The brothers could not manage even that.

source.text: וַיַּחֲלֹ֤ם יוֹסֵף֙ חֲל֔וֹם וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיּוֹסִ֥פוּ ע֖וֹד שְׂנֹ֥א אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And dreamed Joseph a dream and told [it] to his brothers, and they increased again to hate him.

en.L: And Joseph dreamed a dream and told [it] to his brothers, and they hated him still more.
en.B: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, their hatred of him grew worse.
en.R: One night Joseph had a dream. When he told his brothers about it, they hated him even more.

es.L: Y soñó José un sueño y [lo] contó a sus hermanos, y lo odiaron aún más.
es.B: Entonces José tuvo un sueño, y cuando se lo contó a sus hermanos, el odio que le tenían se hizo todavía mayor.
es.R: Una noche José tuvo un sueño. Cuando se lo contó a sus hermanos, lo odiaron todavía más.

fr.L: Et Joseph rêva un rêve et [le] raconta à ses frères, et ils le haïrent encore davantage.
fr.B: Puis Joseph eut un rêve ; quand il le raconta à ses frères, leur haine contre lui s’aggrava.
fr.R: Une nuit, Joseph a fait un rêve. Quand il l’a raconté à ses frères, ils l’ont détesté encore plus.

sw.L: Naye Yusufu akaota ndoto, akawaeleza ndugu zake, nao wakazidi kumchukia.
sw.B: Kisha Yusufu aliota ndoto, na alipowasimulia ndugu zake, chuki yao juu yake ikazidi.
sw.R: Usiku mmoja Yusufu aliota ndoto. Alipowaambia ndugu zake habari zake, walimchukia hata zaidi.

decisions.choice: Joseph dreamed a dream: the first of the dreams that shape his story
decisions.reason: Dreams come in pairs in the Joseph story: two here (verses 5-11), two in prison (40:5), two for Pharaoh (41:1-7). Joseph later says that God gives their meaning (40:8; 41:16).

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֕א הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָלָֽמְתִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, hear, please, this dream which I have dreamed:

en.L: And he said to them, "Please hear this dream that I have dreamed:
en.B: "Listen to this dream I had," he said to them.
en.R: He said to them, "Listen to the dream I had.

es.L: Y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}}, por favor, este sueño que he soñado:
es.B: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} este sueño que tuve», les dijo.
es.R: Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} el sueño que tuve.

fr.L: Et il leur dit : « Écoutez donc ce rêve que j’ai rêvé :
fr.B: « Écoutez le rêve que j’ai fait », leur dit-il.
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Écoutez le rêve que j’ai fait.

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Sikieni, tafadhali, ndoto hii niliyoiota:
sw.B: "Sikilizeni ndoto hii niliyoota," akawaambia.
sw.R: Akawaambia, "Sikilizeni ndoto niliyoota.

source.text: וְ֠הִנֵּה אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מְאַלְּמִ֤ים אֲלֻמִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה קָ֥מָה אֲלֻמָּתִ֖י וְגַם־נִצָּ֑בָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה תְסֻבֶּ֨ינָה֙ אֲלֻמֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַתִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖יןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And behold, we [were] binding sheaves in [the] middle of the field, and behold, arose my sheaf and also stood upright; and behold, gathered round your sheaves and bowed down to my sheaf.

en.L: Look, we were binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and look, my sheaf rose and also stood upright; and look, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf."
en.B: "We were out in the field tying up bundles of grain, when all at once my bundle got up and stood on end, and your bundles came around it and bowed low before it."
en.R: We were in the field, tying stalks of grain into bundles. Suddenly my bundle stood up straight. Then your bundles gathered around it and bowed down to my bundle."

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, nosotros [estábamos] atando gavillas en medio del campo, y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, mi gavilla se levantó y además se quedó derecha; y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} gavillas se pusieron alrededor y se postraron ante mi gavilla».
es.B: «Estábamos en el campo atando gavillas, y de repente mi gavilla se levantó y se quedó en pie, y {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} gavillas se pusieron alrededor de ella y se inclinaron hasta el suelo ante ella».
es.R: Estábamos en el campo, atando el trigo en manojos. De pronto mi manojo se levantó y se quedó derecho. Entonces {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} manojos se pusieron alrededor del mío y se inclinaron ante él».

fr.L: Voici, nous [étions en train de] lier des gerbes au milieu du champ, et voici, ma gerbe s’est levée et s’est même tenue debout ; et voici, vos gerbes l’ont entourée et se sont prosternées devant ma gerbe. »
fr.B: « Nous étions dans les champs à lier des gerbes, quand tout à coup ma gerbe s’est levée et s’est tenue droite, et vos gerbes sont venues l’entourer et se sont prosternées devant elle. »
fr.R: Nous étions dans le champ, et nous attachions les tiges de blé en bottes. Tout à coup, ma botte s’est dressée bien droite. Puis vos bottes se sont mises autour d’elle et se sont inclinées devant ma botte. »

sw.L: Tazama, sisi [tulikuwa] tukifunga miganda katikati ya shamba, na tazama, mganda wangu ukainuka, ukasimama wima pia; na tazama, miganda yenu ikauzunguka, ikasujudu mbele ya mganda wangu."
sw.B: "Tulikuwa shambani tukifunga miganda ya nafaka, ghafla mganda wangu ukainuka ukasimama wima, nayo miganda yenu ikauzunguka na kuuinamia hadi chini."
sw.R: Tulikuwa shambani tukifunga mabua ya nafaka kuwa mafungu. Ghafla fungu langu likasimama wima. Kisha mafungu yenu yakalizunguka, yakainama mbele ya fungu langu."

decisions.choice: bowed down: the gesture of honor to a superior
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when the brothers later bow before Joseph in Egypt (42:6; 43:26; 50:18), where the dream comes true.

decisions.choice: and look ... and look ... and look: the dreamer's vivid telling
decisions.reason: Hinneh, repeated three times, lets the hearers see the dream unfold through the dreamer's eyes.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ אֶחָ֔יו הֲמָלֹ֤ךְ תִּמְלֹךְ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אִם־מָשׁ֥וֹל תִּמְשֹׁ֖ל בָּ֑נוּ וַיּוֹסִ֤פוּ עוֹד֙ שְׂנֹ֣א אֹת֔וֹ עַל־חֲלֹמֹתָ֖יו וְעַל־דְּבָרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him his brothers, really reign will you reign over us, or really rule will you rule over us? And they increased again to hate him on account of his dreams and on account of his words.

en.L: And his brothers said to him, "Will you indeed reign over us? Or will you indeed rule over us?" And they hated him still more for his dreams and for his words.
en.B: His brothers answered, "So you think you will be king over us, do you? Are you going to be our master?" And they hated him all the more because of his dreams and the way he told them.
en.R: His brothers said to him, "Do you really think you will be our king? Will you really rule over us?" So they hated him even more because of his dreams and what he said.

es.L: Y le dijeron sus hermanos: «¿De veras reinarás sobre nosotros? ¿O de veras nos dominarás?». Y lo odiaron aún más por sus sueños y por sus palabras.
es.B: Sus hermanos le contestaron: «¿Así que crees que vas a ser rey sobre nosotros? ¿Vas a ser nuestro amo?». Y lo odiaron todavía más por sus sueños y por la manera en que los contaba.
es.R: Sus hermanos le dijeron: «¿De verdad piensas que vas a ser nuestro rey? ¿De verdad nos vas a mandar?». Así que lo odiaron todavía más por sus sueños y por lo que decía.

fr.L: Et ses frères lui dirent : « Régneras-tu vraiment sur nous ? Ou bien domineras-tu vraiment sur nous ? » Et ils le haïrent encore davantage à cause de ses rêves et à cause de ses paroles.
fr.B: Ses frères lui répondirent : « Alors tu crois que tu seras roi sur nous ? Tu vas devenir notre maître ? » Et ils le haïrent d’autant plus, à cause de ses rêves et de la manière dont il les racontait.
fr.R: Ses frères lui ont dit : « Tu crois vraiment que tu vas être notre roi ? Tu vas vraiment nous commander ? » Alors ils l’ont détesté encore plus, à cause de ses rêves et de ce qu’il disait.

sw.L: Nao ndugu zake wakamwambia, "Je, kweli utatawala juu yetu? Au kweli utatumiliki?" Nao wakazidi kumchukia kwa sababu ya ndoto zake na kwa sababu ya maneno yake.
sw.B: Ndugu zake wakamjibu, "Kumbe unadhani utakuwa mfalme juu yetu? Utakuwa bwana wetu, sivyo?" Wakazidi kumchukia kwa sababu ya ndoto zake na jinsi alivyozisimulia.
sw.R: Ndugu zake wakamwambia, "Unafikiri kweli utakuwa mfalme wetu? Kweli utatutawala?" Kwa hiyo walimchukia hata zaidi kwa sababu ya ndoto zake na maneno aliyosema.

decisions.choice: will you indeed reign ... indeed rule: scornful emphasis
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for emphasis, and the questions are sarcastic. Without knowing it, the brothers name what will happen.

decisions.choice: his words: what he said, the telling of the dreams
decisions.reason: Not only the dreams but Joseph's telling of them angered his brothers.

source.text: וַיַּחֲלֹ֥ם עוֹד֙ חֲל֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה חָלַ֤מְתִּֽי חֲלוֹם֙ ע֔וֹד וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֖ים לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he dreamed again another dream and recounted it to his brothers and said, behold, I have dreamed a dream again, and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars [were] bowing down to me.

en.L: And he dreamed yet another dream and told it to his brothers and said, "Look, I have dreamed another dream: and look, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
en.B: Then he had a second dream and told that one to his brothers as well. "Listen," he said, "I have had another dream. This time the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing to me."
en.R: Later Joseph had another dream, and he told his brothers about it too. He said, "I had another dream. The sun, the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."

es.L: Y soñó todavía otro sueño y se lo contó a sus hermanos, y dijo: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, he soñado otro sueño: y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, el sol y la luna y once estrellas se postraban ante mí».
es.B: Después tuvo un segundo sueño, y también se lo contó a sus hermanos. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, he tenido otro sueño. Esta vez el sol, la luna y once estrellas se inclinaban ante mí».
es.R: Más tarde José tuvo otro sueño, y también se lo contó a sus hermanos. Les dijo: «Tuve otro sueño. El sol, la luna y once estrellas se inclinaban ante mí».

fr.L: Et il rêva encore un autre rêve et le raconta à ses frères, et il dit : « Voici, j’ai rêvé encore un rêve : et voici, le soleil et la lune et onze étoiles se prosternaient devant moi. »
fr.B: Puis il eut un second rêve, qu’il raconta aussi à ses frères. « Écoutez, dit-il, j’ai fait un autre rêve. Cette fois, le soleil, la lune et onze étoiles se prosternaient devant moi. »
fr.R: Plus tard, Joseph a fait un autre rêve, et il l’a aussi raconté à ses frères. Il a dit : « J’ai fait un autre rêve. Le soleil, la lune et onze étoiles s’inclinaient devant moi. »

sw.L: Naye akaota tena ndoto nyingine, akawasimulia ndugu zake, akasema, "Tazama, nimeota ndoto tena: na tazama, jua na mwezi na nyota kumi na moja zilikuwa zikinisujudia."
sw.B: Kisha akaota ndoto ya pili, akawasimulia ndugu zake pia. Akasema, "Sikilizeni, nimeota ndoto nyingine. Safari hii jua, mwezi na nyota kumi na moja zilikuwa zikiniinamia."
sw.R: Baadaye Yusufu aliota ndoto nyingine, naye akawaambia ndugu zake habari zake pia. Akasema, "Nimeota ndoto nyingine. Jua, mwezi na nyota kumi na moja zilikuwa zikiniinamia."

decisions.choice: the sun, the moon and eleven stars: his father, his mother and his eleven brothers
decisions.reason: Jacob reads the dream so at once (verse 10). The second dream reaches beyond the field into the sky and includes the parents.

source.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר אֶל־אָבִיו֮ וְאֶל־אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּגְעַר־בּ֣וֹ אָבִ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he recounted [it] to his father and to his brothers, and rebuked him his father and said to him, what [is] this dream which you have dreamed? Really come will we come, I and your mother and your brothers, to bow down to you to [the] ground?

en.L: And he told [it] to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him, "What [is] this dream that you have dreamed? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the ground before you?"
en.B: When he told it to his father as well as his brothers, his father scolded him. "What sort of dream is this?" he said. "Are your mother and I and your brothers really going to come and bow to the ground in front of you?"
en.R: He told the dream to his father and his brothers. But his father scolded him. "What kind of dream is this?" he asked. "Will your mother and I and your brothers really come and bow down to the ground in front of you?"

es.L: Y [lo] contó a su padre y a sus hermanos, y su padre lo reprendió y le dijo: «¿Qué [es] este sueño que has soñado? ¿De veras vendremos yo y tu madre y tus hermanos a postrarnos en tierra ante ti?».
es.B: Cuando se lo contó a su padre además de a sus hermanos, su padre lo regañó y le dijo: «¿Qué clase de sueño es este? ¿De verdad vamos a venir tu madre, yo y tus hermanos a inclinarnos hasta el suelo delante de ti?».
es.R: José les contó el sueño a su padre y a sus hermanos. Pero su padre lo regañó. Le preguntó: «¿Qué sueño es ese? ¿De verdad tu madre, yo y tus hermanos vamos a venir a inclinarnos hasta el suelo delante de ti?».

fr.L: Et il [le] raconta à son père et à ses frères, et son père le réprimanda et lui dit : « Qu’[est-ce que] ce rêve que tu as rêvé ? Viendrons-nous vraiment, moi et ta mère et tes frères, nous prosterner devant toi jusqu’à terre ? »
fr.B: Quand il le raconta à son père aussi bien qu’à ses frères, son père le gronda et lui dit : « Qu’est-ce que c’est que ce rêve ? Ta mère, moi et tes frères, allons-nous vraiment venir nous prosterner jusqu’à terre devant toi ? »
fr.R: Joseph a raconté son rêve à son père et à ses frères. Mais son père l’a grondé. Il lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que c’est que ce rêve ? Est-ce que ta mère, moi et tes frères, nous allons vraiment venir nous incliner jusqu’au sol devant toi ? »

sw.L: Naye akawasimulia baba yake na ndugu zake, naye baba yake akamkemea, akamwambia, "Ni ndoto gani hii uliyoota? Je, kweli tutakuja, mimi na mama yako na ndugu zako, kukusujudia hadi chini?"
sw.B: Alipomsimulia baba yake pamoja na ndugu zake, baba yake akamkaripia, akasema, "Ndoto gani hii? Kweli mimi na mama yako na ndugu zako tutakuja kukuinamia hadi chini mbele yako?"
sw.R: Yusufu aliwaeleza baba yake na ndugu zake ile ndoto. Lakini baba yake alimkaripia. Akamwuliza, "Ni ndoto ya namna gani hii? Je, kweli mimi na mama yako na ndugu zako tutakuja kukuinamia hadi chini?"

decisions.choice: your mother: Rachel, though she has died (35:19)
alternatives: Leah, as the mother of the household
a figure for the family as a whole
decisions.reason: Rachel's death has already been told. Jacob may mean the family as a whole, or the dream may simply include her; the text does not explain.

source.text: וַיְקַנְאוּ־ב֖וֹ אֶחָ֑יו וְאָבִ֖יו שָׁמַ֥ר אֶת־הַדָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And were jealous of him his brothers, and his father kept the matter.

en.L: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter [in mind].
en.B: His brothers envied him, but his father did not forget what he had said.
en.R: His brothers were jealous of Joseph. But his father kept thinking about what Joseph had said.

es.L: Y sus hermanos le tuvieron envidia, pero su padre guardó el asunto [en la memoria].
es.B: Sus hermanos le tenían envidia, pero su padre no olvidó lo que había dicho.
es.R: Sus hermanos tenían celos de José. Pero su padre seguía pensando en lo que José había dicho.

fr.L: Et ses frères furent jaloux de lui, mais son père garda la chose [en mémoire].
fr.B: Ses frères l’envièrent, mais son père n’oublia pas ce qu’il avait dit.
fr.R: Les frères de Joseph étaient jaloux de lui. Mais son père a continué à réfléchir à ce que Joseph avait dit.

sw.L: Nao ndugu zake wakamwonea wivu, lakini baba yake akalishika jambo hilo [moyoni].
sw.B: Ndugu zake walimwonea wivu, lakini baba yake hakulisahau jambo alilosema.
sw.R: Ndugu zake Yusufu walimwonea wivu. Lakini baba yake aliendelea kufikiri juu ya maneno ya Yusufu.

decisions.choice: kept the matter: kept it in mind, waiting to see
decisions.reason: Jacob rebukes Joseph aloud but holds on to the dream, wondering what it means (compare Luke 2:19).

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶחָ֑יו לִרְע֛וֹת אֶׄתׄ־צֹ֥אןאֲבִיהֶ֖ם בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And went his brothers to pasture [the] flock of their father at Shechem.

en.L: And his brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem.
en.B: One time his brothers had gone to graze their father's flocks near Shechem.
en.R: Joseph's brothers went to Shechem to find grass for their father's sheep and goats.

es.L: Y fueron sus hermanos a apacentar el rebaño de su padre en Siquem.
es.B: En cierta ocasión, sus hermanos habían ido a pastorear los rebaños de su padre cerca de Siquem.
es.R: Los hermanos de José se fueron a Siquem a buscar pasto para las ovejas y las cabras de su padre.

fr.L: Et ses frères allèrent faire paître le troupeau de leur père à Sichem.
fr.B: Un jour, ses frères étaient partis faire paître les troupeaux de leur père près de Sichem.
fr.R: Les frères de Joseph sont allés à Sichem pour trouver de l’herbe pour les moutons et les chèvres de leur père.

sw.L: Nao ndugu zake wakaenda kulisha kundi la baba yao huko Shekemu.
sw.B: Wakati mmoja ndugu zake walikuwa wameenda kuchunga makundi ya baba yao karibu na Shekemu.
sw.R: Ndugu zake Yusufu walikwenda Shekemu kutafuta majani kwa ajili ya kondoo na mbuzi wa baba yao.

decisions.choice: at Shechem: where the brothers had killed the men of the city
decisions.reason: Shechem was about 50 miles (80 km) north of Hebron, and the place of the massacre in chapter 34. Sending Joseph there alone was not without risk.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם לְכָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ הִנֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Israel to Joseph, [are] not your brothers pasturing at Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them. And he said to him, here I [am].

en.L: And Israel said to Joseph, "Are not your brothers pasturing [the flock] at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them." And he said to him, "Here I am."
en.B: Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are grazing the flocks near Shechem, are they not? Come, I am going to send you to them." "I am ready," Joseph replied.
en.R: Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are taking care of the sheep and goats near Shechem. I want you to go to them." Joseph answered, "I will go."

es.L: Y dijo Israel a José: «¿No están tus hermanos apacentando [el rebaño] en Siquem? Ven, y te enviaré a ellos». Y él le dijo: «Aquí estoy».
es.B: Israel le dijo a José: «Tus hermanos están pastoreando los rebaños cerca de Siquem, ¿no es así? Ven, que te voy a enviar adonde están ellos». «Estoy listo», respondió José.
es.R: Israel le dijo a José: «Tus hermanos están cuidando las ovejas y las cabras cerca de Siquem. Quiero que vayas a verlos». José le contestó: «Iré».

fr.L: Et Israël dit à Joseph : « Tes frères ne font-ils pas paître [le troupeau] à Sichem ? Viens, je vais t’envoyer vers eux. » Et il lui dit : « Me voici. »
fr.B: Israël dit à Joseph : « Tes frères font paître les troupeaux près de Sichem, n’est-ce pas ? Viens, je vais t’envoyer auprès d’eux. » « Je suis prêt », répondit Joseph.
fr.R: Israël a dit à Joseph : « Tes frères s’occupent des moutons et des chèvres près de Sichem. Je veux que tu ailles les voir. » Joseph a répondu : « J’y vais. »

sw.L: Naye Israeli akamwambia Yusufu, "Je, ndugu zako hawalishi [kundi] huko Shekemu? Njoo, nami nitakutuma kwao." Naye akamwambia, "Mimi hapa."
sw.B: Israeli akamwambia Yusufu, "Ndugu zako wanachunga makundi karibu na Shekemu, sivyo? Njoo, nataka kukutuma kwao." Yusufu akajibu, "Niko tayari."
sw.R: Israeli alimwambia Yusufu, "Ndugu zako wanachunga kondoo na mbuzi karibu na Shekemu. Nataka uende kwao." Yusufu akajibu, "Nitakwenda."

decisions.choice: here I am: ready to do what is asked
decisions.reason: The same answer Abraham gives when called (22:1, 11). It expresses readiness to obey.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ־נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת־שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ וְאֶת־שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֵ֖נִי דָּבָ֑ר וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֨הוּ֙ מֵעֵ֣מֶק חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א שְׁכֶֽמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, go, please, see [the] welfare of your brothers and [the] welfare of the flock, and bring back to me word. And he sent him from [the] valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

en.L: And he said to him, "Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers and well with the flock, and bring me word." So he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
en.B: "Go and find out how your brothers are doing and how the flocks are," he said, "and come back and tell me." So he sent him off from the valley of Hebron, and Joseph made his way to Shechem.
en.R: Israel said, "Go and see if your brothers and the animals are all right. Then come back and tell me." So Israel sent him from the valley of Hebron, and Joseph went to Shechem.

es.L: Y le dijo: «Ve, por favor, mira si están bien tus hermanos y si está bien el rebaño, y tráeme noticias». Y lo envió desde el valle de Hebrón, y llegó a Siquem.
es.B: «Ve a ver cómo están tus hermanos y cómo están los rebaños, y vuelve a contármelo», le dijo. Así que lo envió desde el valle de Hebrón, y José se dirigió a Siquem.
es.R: Israel le dijo: «Ve a ver si tus hermanos y los animales están bien. Después vuelve y cuéntamelo». Entonces Israel lo envió desde el valle de Hebrón, y José se fue a Siquem.

fr.L: Et il lui dit : « Va donc, vois si tout va bien pour tes frères et si tout va bien pour le troupeau, et rapporte-moi des nouvelles. » Et il l’envoya de la vallée d’Hébron, et il arriva à Sichem.
fr.B: « Va voir comment se portent tes frères et comment va le troupeau, lui dit-il, et reviens me donner des nouvelles. » Il l’envoya donc de la vallée d’Hébron, et Joseph se rendit à Sichem.
fr.R: Israël lui a dit : « Va voir si tout va bien pour tes frères et pour les bêtes. Ensuite, reviens me le dire. » Israël l’a donc envoyé de la vallée d’Hébron, et Joseph est allé à Sichem.

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Nenda basi, ukaone kama ndugu zako ni salama na kama kundi ni salama, uniletee habari." Basi akamtuma kutoka bonde la Hebroni, naye akafika Shekemu.
sw.B: Akamwambia, "Nenda ukaone ndugu zako wanaendeleaje na makundi yako hali gani, kisha urudi uniambie." Basi akamtuma kutoka bonde la Hebroni, naye Yusufu akaenda mpaka Shekemu.
sw.R: Israeli akasema, "Nenda ukaone kama ndugu zako na wanyama wako salama. Kisha urudi uniambie." Kwa hiyo Israeli alimtuma kutoka bonde la Hebroni, naye Yusufu akaenda Shekemu.

decisions.choice: the welfare (shalom) of your brothers
decisions.reason: The word shalom echoes verse 4: the brothers could not speak to Joseph with shalom, and now he is sent to see about their shalom.

source.text: וַיִּמְצָאֵ֣הוּ אִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה תֹעֶ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֧הוּ הָאִ֛ישׁ לֵאמֹ֖ר מַה־תְּבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And found him a man, and behold, [he was] wandering in the field; and asked him the man, saying, what are you seeking?

en.L: And a man found him, and look, he was wandering in the open country; and the man asked him, saying, "What are you seeking?"
en.B: A man came upon him wandering around in the countryside and asked him, "What are you looking for?"
en.R: A man found Joseph wandering around in the fields. The man asked him, "What are you looking for?"

es.L: Y lo encontró un hombre, y he aquí que andaba errante por el campo; y le preguntó el hombre, diciendo: «¿Qué buscas?».
es.B: Un hombre lo encontró vagando por el campo y le preguntó: «¿Qué andas buscando?».
es.R: Un hombre encontró a José dando vueltas por el campo. El hombre le preguntó: «¿Qué estás buscando?».

fr.L: Et un homme le trouva, et voici, il errait dans la campagne ; et l’homme l’interrogea, disant : « Que cherches-tu ? »
fr.B: Un homme le rencontra qui errait dans la campagne et lui demanda : « Que cherches-tu ? »
fr.R: Un homme a trouvé Joseph qui marchait au hasard dans les champs. L’homme lui a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que tu cherches ? »

sw.L: Naye mtu mmoja akamkuta, na tazama, alikuwa akitangatanga kondeni; naye yule mtu akamwuliza, akisema, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.B: Mtu mmoja alimkuta akizungukazunguka mashambani, akamwuliza, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alimkuta Yusufu akitembea huku na huko mashambani. Yule mtu akamwuliza, "Unatafuta nini?"

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־אַחַ֖י אָנֹכִ֣י מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ הַגִּֽידָה־נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵיפֹ֖ה הֵ֥ם רֹעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, my brothers I [am] seeking; tell, please, to me where they [are] pasturing.

en.L: And he said, "I am seeking my brothers. Please tell me where they are pasturing [the flock]."
en.B: "It is my brothers I am trying to find," he answered. "Can you tell me where they are grazing their flocks?"
en.R: Joseph answered, "I am looking for my brothers. Can you tell me where they are with their sheep and goats?"

es.L: Y él dijo: «A mis hermanos busco; dime, por favor, dónde están apacentando [el rebaño]».
es.B: «Estoy buscando a mis hermanos», respondió. «¿Podrías decirme dónde están pastoreando sus rebaños?».
es.R: José le contestó: «Busco a mis hermanos. ¿Puedes decirme dónde están con sus ovejas y sus cabras?».

fr.L: Et il dit : « Ce sont mes frères que je cherche. Dis-moi donc où ils font paître [le troupeau]. »
fr.B: « Ce sont mes frères que je cherche, répondit-il. Peux-tu me dire où ils font paître leurs troupeaux ? »
fr.R: Joseph a répondu : « Je cherche mes frères. Est-ce que tu peux me dire où ils sont avec leurs moutons et leurs chèvres ? »

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Ndugu zangu ndio ninaowatafuta. Tafadhali niambie wanalisha [kundi] wapi."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Ninawatafuta ndugu zangu. Waweza kuniambia wanachunga makundi yao wapi?"
sw.R: Yusufu akajibu, "Ninawatafuta ndugu zangu. Unaweza kuniambia wako wapi na kondoo na mbuzi wao?"

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ נָסְע֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה דֹּתָ֑יְנָה וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יוֹסֵף֙ אַחַ֣ר אֶחָ֔יו וַיִּמְצָאֵ֖ם בְּדֹתָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the man, they have set out from here, for I heard [them] saying, let us go to Dothan. And went Joseph after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

en.L: And the man said, "They have moved on from here, for I heard [them] saying, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
en.B: "They have left here," the man said. "I heard them say, 'Let us go on to Dothan.'" So Joseph followed his brothers and caught up with them at Dothan.
en.R: The man said, "They left this place. I heard them say, 'Let us go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

es.L: Y dijo el hombre: «Se han ido de aquí, porque [los] oí decir: “Vamos a Dotán”». Y fue José tras sus hermanos y los encontró en Dotán.
es.B: «Se marcharon de aquí», dijo el hombre. «Los oí decir: “Sigamos hasta Dotán”». Así que José siguió a sus hermanos y los alcanzó en Dotán.
es.R: El hombre le dijo: «Se fueron de aquí. Los oí decir: “Vamos a Dotán”». Entonces José fue tras sus hermanos y los encontró en Dotán.

fr.L: Et l’homme dit : « Ils sont partis d’ici, car je [les] ai entendus dire : “Allons à Dothan.” » Et Joseph alla après ses frères et les trouva à Dothan.
fr.B: « Ils sont partis d’ici, dit l’homme. Je les ai entendus dire : “Allons jusqu’à Dothan.” » Joseph suivit donc ses frères et les rejoignit à Dothan.
fr.R: L’homme a dit : « Ils sont partis d’ici. Je les ai entendus dire : “Allons à Dothan.” » Alors Joseph est parti à la suite de ses frères, et il les a trouvés à Dothan.

sw.L: Naye yule mtu akasema, "Wameondoka hapa, kwa maana niliwasikia wakisema, 'Twendeni Dothani.'" Basi Yusufu akawafuata ndugu zake, akawakuta huko Dothani.
sw.B: Yule mtu akasema, "Wameshaondoka hapa. Niliwasikia wakisema, 'Tuendelee mpaka Dothani.'" Basi Yusufu akawafuata ndugu zake, akawapata huko Dothani.
sw.R: Yule mtu akasema, "Waliondoka mahali hapa. Niliwasikia wakisema, 'Twende Dothani.'" Kwa hiyo Yusufu aliwafuata ndugu zake, akawakuta Dothani.

decisions.choice: Dothan: a town on the trade route to Egypt
decisions.reason: Dothan lay about 15 miles (24 km) north of Shechem, near the road that ran from Gilead down to the coast and on to Egypt, which explains the caravan in verse 25.

source.text: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּבְטֶ֨רֶם֙ יִקְרַ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽתְנַכְּל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they saw him from a distance, and before he drew near to them, and they plotted against him to kill him.

en.L: And they saw him from afar, and before he came near to them they plotted against him to kill him.
en.B: They spotted him while he was still far off, and before he reached them they schemed to put him to death.
en.R: The brothers saw Joseph coming from far away. Before he got to them, they made a plan to kill him.

es.L: Y lo vieron de lejos, y antes de que se acercara a ellos, conspiraron contra él para matarlo.
es.B: Lo divisaron cuando todavía estaba lejos, y antes de que llegara hasta ellos tramaron darle muerte.
es.R: Los hermanos vieron venir a José desde lejos. Antes de que llegara adonde estaban, hicieron un plan para matarlo.

fr.L: Et ils le virent de loin, et avant qu’il ne s’approche d’eux, ils complotèrent contre lui pour le faire mourir.
fr.B: Ils l’aperçurent alors qu’il était encore loin, et avant qu’il ne les ait rejoints, ils formèrent le projet de le mettre à mort.
fr.R: Les frères ont vu Joseph arriver de loin. Avant qu’il arrive près d’eux, ils ont fait un plan pour le tuer.

sw.L: Nao wakamwona kwa mbali, na kabla hajawakaribia, wakafanya shauri juu yake ili kumwua.
sw.B: Walimwona alipokuwa bado mbali, na kabla hajawafikia wakapanga njama ya kumwua.
sw.R: Ndugu zake walimwona Yusufu akija kutoka mbali. Kabla hajawafikia, walipanga mpango wa kumwua.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו הִנֵּ֗ה בַּ֛עַל הַחֲלֹמ֥וֹת הַלָּזֶ֖ה בָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said each to his brother, behold, [the] master of the dreams, this [one], is coming.

en.L: And they said to one another, "Look, this master of dreams is coming.
en.B: "Here comes the great dreamer," they said to one another.
en.R: They said to each other, "Look, here comes the dreamer!

es.L: Y se dijeron el uno al otro: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, viene este señor de los sueños.
es.B: «Ahí viene el gran soñador», se dijeron unos a otros.
es.R: Se dijeron unos a otros: «¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, ahí viene el soñador!

fr.L: Et ils se dirent l’un à l’autre : « Voici, ce maître des rêves arrive.
fr.B: « Voici venir le grand rêveur », se dirent-ils les uns aux autres.
fr.R: Ils se sont dit entre eux : « Regardez, voilà le rêveur qui arrive !

sw.L: Nao wakaambiana, "Tazama, bwana huyu wa ndoto anakuja.
sw.B: "Tazameni, yule bingwa wa ndoto anakuja," wakaambiana.
sw.R: Wakaambiana, "Angalieni, yule mwota ndoto anakuja!

decisions.choice: master of dreams: a mocking title
decisions.reason: "Master (ba'al) of dreams" means one who specializes in dreams. The brothers use it with contempt.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת וְאָמַ֕רְנוּ חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ וְנִרְאֶ֕ה מַה־יִּהְי֖וּ חֲלֹמֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And now come, and let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say, an animal, wild, has eaten him; and we will see what will be his dreams.

en.L: Now come, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits; and we will say, 'A wild animal has devoured him.' And we will see what will become of his dreams."
en.B: "Come on, let us kill him now and toss him into one of these cisterns. We can say a wild beast ate him. Then we will find out what comes of his dreams!"
en.R: Come on, let us kill him and throw his body into one of these empty wells. We can say that a wild animal ate him. Then we will see what happens to his dreams!"

es.L: Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, matémoslo y echémoslo en uno de los pozos, y diremos: “Una fiera lo devoró”. Y veremos qué será de sus sueños».
es.B: «Vamos, matémoslo ahora y arrojémoslo a una de estas cisternas. Podemos decir que una fiera lo devoró. ¡Entonces veremos en qué paran sus sueños!».
es.R: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, matémoslo y echemos su cuerpo en uno de estos pozos vacíos. Podemos decir que un animal salvaje se lo comió. ¡Entonces veremos qué pasa con sus sueños!».

fr.L: Et maintenant, venez, tuons-le et jetons-le dans l’une des fosses ; et nous dirons : “Une bête sauvage l’a dévoré.” Et nous verrons ce que deviendront ses rêves. »
fr.B: « Allons, tuons-le tout de suite et jetons-le dans une de ces citernes. Nous dirons qu’une bête féroce l’a dévoré. On verra bien alors ce qu’il advient de ses rêves ! »
fr.R: Venez, tuons-le et jetons son corps dans un de ces puits vides. Nous dirons qu’une bête sauvage l’a mangé. Alors nous verrons bien ce qui arrivera à ses rêves ! »

sw.L: Basi sasa njooni, tumwue na kumtupa katika mojawapo ya mashimo haya; nasi tutasema, 'Mnyama wa mwitu amemla.' Nasi tutaona ndoto zake zitakuwaje."
sw.B: "Haya, tumwue sasa hivi tumtupe katika mojawapo ya mashimo haya ya maji. Tunaweza kusema kwamba mnyama mkali amemla. Ndipo tutakapoona ndoto zake zitaishia wapi!"
sw.R: Njooni, tumwue na kuutupa mwili wake katika kimojawapo cha visima hivi vikavu. Tunaweza kusema kwamba mnyama wa porini amemla. Kisha tutaona kitakachotokea kwa ndoto zake!"

decisions.choice: the pits: cisterns cut in the rock
decisions.reason: A bor was a pit dug to catch rainwater, usually bottle-shaped, so that a person thrown in could not climb out. In the dry season it might be empty (verse 24).

decisions.choice: empty wells
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word; verse 24 says the pit was empty.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיַּצִּלֵ֖הוּ מִיָּדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נַכֶּ֖נּוּ נָֽפֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Reuben and rescued him from their hand and said, let us not strike him [as to] life.

en.L: And Reuben heard [it] and rescued him from their hand and said, "Let us not take his life."
en.B: When Reuben heard this, he tried to save Joseph from them. "We must not kill him," he said.
en.R: But Reuben heard what they said, and he tried to save Joseph from them. He said, "Let us not kill him."

es.L: Y oyó Rubén [esto] y lo libró de sus manos, y dijo: «No le quitemos la vida».
es.B: Cuando Rubén oyó esto, trató de salvar a José de ellos. «No debemos matarlo», dijo.
es.R: Pero Rubén oyó lo que decían y trató de salvar a José. Les dijo: «No lo matemos».

fr.L: Et Ruben [l’]entendit, et il le délivra de leur main, et il dit : « Ne lui ôtons pas la vie. »
fr.B: Quand Ruben entendit cela, il chercha à sauver Joseph de leurs mains. « Il ne faut pas le tuer », dit-il.
fr.R: Mais Ruben a entendu ce qu’ils disaient, et il a essayé de sauver Joseph. Il a dit : « Ne le tuons pas. »

sw.L: Naye Reubeni akasikia, akamwokoa mikononi mwao, akasema, "Tusimtoe uhai."
sw.B: Reubeni aliposikia hayo, alijaribu kumwokoa Yusufu mikononi mwao. Akasema, "Hatupaswi kumwua."
sw.R: Lakini Reubeni alisikia walichosema, akajaribu kumwokoa Yusufu. Akasema, "Tusimwue."

decisions.choice: rescued him: Reuben set out to save him
decisions.reason: The verb states the result Reuben aimed at; verse 22 shows that his plan was to come back later and take Joseph home.

decisions.choice: strike him as to life: kill him
decisions.reason: To strike someone "in the life (nefesh)" is to kill.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֣ם׀רְאוּבֵן֮ אַל־תִּשְׁפְּכוּ־דָם֒ הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל־תִּשְׁלְחוּ־ב֑וֹ לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל־אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Reuben, do not shed blood; throw him into this pit which [is] in the wilderness, and a hand do not stretch out on him, so as to rescue him from their hand, to restore him to his father.

en.L: And Reuben said to them, "Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit here in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him." He said this so that he might rescue him from their hand and bring him back to his father.
en.B: "Do not shed his blood," Reuben told them. "Throw him into this cistern out here in the wild, but do not lay a hand on him." He meant to rescue him from them and take him back to his father.
en.R: "Do not spill his blood," Reuben told them. "Just throw him into this well here in the desert. But do not hurt him." Reuben planned to save Joseph and take him back to his father.

es.L: Y les dijo Rubén: «No {{plural_you:derramen|derraméis}} sangre; {{plural_you:échenlo|echadlo}} en este pozo que [está] en el desierto, pero no {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} la mano sobre él». [Decía esto] para librarlo de sus manos y devolverlo a su padre.
es.B: «No {{plural_you:derramen|derraméis}} su sangre», les dijo Rubén. «{{plural_you:Échenlo|Echadlo}} en esta cisterna, aquí en el desierto, pero no le {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} la mano encima». Lo que quería era librarlo de ellos y llevarlo de vuelta a su padre.
es.R: «No {{plural_you:derramen|derraméis}} su sangre», les dijo Rubén. «Solo {{plural_you:échenlo|echadlo}} en este pozo, aquí en el desierto. Pero no le {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} daño». Rubén pensaba salvar a José y llevarlo de vuelta con su padre.

fr.L: Et Ruben leur dit : « Ne versez pas de sang. Jetez-le dans cette fosse qui [est] dans le désert, mais ne portez pas la main sur lui. » [Il parlait ainsi] afin de le délivrer de leur main, pour le ramener à son père.
fr.B: « Ne versez pas son sang, leur dit Ruben. Jetez-le dans cette citerne, ici dans le désert, mais ne portez pas la main sur lui. » Il voulait le délivrer de leurs mains et le ramener à son père.
fr.R: Ruben leur a dit : « Ne faites pas couler son sang. Jetez-le seulement dans ce puits, ici dans le désert. Mais ne lui faites pas de mal. » Ruben pensait sauver Joseph et le ramener à son père.

sw.L: Naye Reubeni akawaambia, "Msimwage damu; mtupeni katika shimo hili lililoko nyikani, lakini msinyoshe mkono juu yake." [Alisema hivyo] ili amwokoe mikononi mwao, amrudishe kwa baba yake.
sw.B: Reubeni akawaambia, "Msimwage damu yake. Mtupeni katika shimo hili la maji hapa nyikani, lakini msimguse kwa mkono." Alikusudia kumwokoa mikononi mwao na kumrudisha kwa baba yake.
sw.R: Reubeni akawaambia, "Msimwage damu yake. Mtupeni tu katika kisima hiki hapa jangwani. Lakini msimdhuru." Reubeni alipanga kumwokoa Yusufu na kumrudisha kwa baba yake.

decisions.choice: so as to rescue him: the narrator tells Reuben's hidden purpose
decisions.reason: The last part of the verse is not spoken aloud; it explains why Reuben proposed the pit. As the oldest son, he would answer to Jacob for the boy.

source.text: וַֽיְהִ֕י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־בָּ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־אֶחָ֑יו וַיַּפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־כֻּתָּנְתּ֔וֹ אֶת־כְּתֹ֥נֶת הַפַּסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when came Joseph to his brothers, and they stripped Joseph [of] his tunic, [the] tunic of the palms which [was] on him,

en.L: And it happened, when Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles] that [was] on him,
en.B: So when Joseph reached his brothers, they tore off his robe, the long-sleeved robe he was wearing,
en.R: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his robe, the special robe with long sleeves that he was wearing.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando llegó José a sus hermanos, despojaron a José de su túnica, la túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos] que [llevaba] sobre sí,
es.B: Así que, cuando José llegó adonde estaban sus hermanos, le arrancaron la túnica, la túnica larga con mangas que llevaba puesta,
es.R: Cuando José llegó adonde estaban sus hermanos, le quitaron la túnica, la túnica especial de mangas largas que llevaba puesta.

fr.L: Et il arriva, lorsque Joseph vint vers ses frères, qu’ils dépouillèrent Joseph de sa tunique, la tunique [qui descendait jusqu’aux] poignets [et aux chevilles], qui [était] sur lui,
fr.B: Aussi, dès que Joseph eut rejoint ses frères, ils lui arrachèrent sa tunique, la longue tunique à manches qu’il portait,
fr.R: Quand Joseph est arrivé près de ses frères, ils lui ont enlevé sa tunique, la belle tunique à longues manches qu’il portait.

sw.L: Ikawa, Yusufu alipowafikia ndugu zake, wakamvua Yusufu kanzu yake, kanzu [iliyofika hadi] vifundo [vya mikono na miguu] aliyokuwa ameivaa,
sw.B: Basi Yusufu alipowafikia ndugu zake, walimvua kanzu yake, ile kanzu ndefu yenye mikono mirefu aliyokuwa ameivaa,
sw.R: Yusufu alipowafikia ndugu zake, walimvua kanzu yake, ile kanzu ya pekee yenye mikono mirefu aliyokuwa ameivaa.

decisions.choice: his tunic, the long tunic: the sign of favor is the first thing taken
decisions.reason: The narrator names the robe twice. Clothing marks each turn in Joseph's story: this robe, the garment left with Potiphar's wife (39:12), and the fine linen Pharaoh gives him (41:42).

source.text: וַיִּ֨קָּחֻ֔הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ הַבֹּ֑רָה וְהַבּ֣וֹר רֵ֔ק אֵ֥ין בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: and they took him and threw him into the pit; and the pit [was] empty, there [was] not in it water.

en.L: and they took him and threw him into the pit. And the pit [was] empty; [there was] no water in it.
en.B: and they grabbed him and threw him into the cistern. The cistern was empty; it had no water in it.
en.R: They grabbed him and threw him into the well. The well was empty. There was no water in it.

es.L: y lo tomaron y lo echaron en el pozo. Y el pozo [estaba] vacío; no [había] agua en él.
es.B: y lo agarraron y lo arrojaron a la cisterna. La cisterna estaba vacía; no tenía agua.
es.R: Lo agarraron y lo echaron al pozo. El pozo estaba vacío. No tenía agua.

fr.L: et ils le prirent et le jetèrent dans la fosse. Et la fosse [était] vide ; [il n’y avait] pas d’eau dedans.
fr.B: et ils se saisirent de lui et le jetèrent dans la citerne. La citerne était vide, il n’y avait pas d’eau.
fr.R: Ils ont attrapé Joseph et l’ont jeté dans le puits. Le puits était vide. Il n’y avait pas d’eau dedans.

sw.L: nao wakamchukua wakamtupa shimoni. Na shimo [lilikuwa] tupu; halikuwa na maji ndani yake.
sw.B: wakamkamata wakamtupa ndani ya shimo la maji. Shimo hilo lilikuwa tupu; halikuwa na maji ndani yake.
sw.R: Walimkamata Yusufu wakamtupa kisimani. Kisima kilikuwa kikavu. Hakikuwa na maji ndani yake.

source.text: וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֮ לֶֽאֱכָל־לֶחֶם֒ וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְא֔וּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֹרְחַ֣ת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים בָּאָ֖ה מִגִּלְעָ֑ד וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֣ם נֹֽשְׂאִ֗ים נְכֹאת֙ וּצְרִ֣י וָלֹ֔ט הוֹלְכִ֖ים לְהוֹרִ֥יד מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sat down to eat bread, and they lifted their eyes and saw, and behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites [was] coming from Gilead, and their camels [were] carrying spice and balm and myrrh, traveling to take [them] down to Egypt.

en.L: And they sat down to eat bread. And they lifted up their eyes and looked, and look, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying gum, balm and myrrh, on their way to take [it] down to Egypt.
en.B: Then they sat down to their meal. Looking up, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, their camels loaded with gum, balm and resin, which they were taking down to Egypt.
en.R: Then the brothers sat down to eat. They looked up and saw a group of Ishmaelite traders coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices and sweet-smelling gums to sell in Egypt.

es.L: Y se sentaron a comer pan. Y alzaron sus ojos y miraron, y he aquí que una caravana de ismaelitas venía de Galaad, y sus camellos llevaban goma, bálsamo y mirra; iban de camino para bajar[los] a Egipto.
es.B: Luego se sentaron a comer. Al levantar la vista, vieron una caravana de ismaelitas que venía de Galaad, con sus camellos cargados de goma, bálsamo y resina, que llevaban a Egipto.
es.R: Después los hermanos se sentaron a comer. Miraron y vieron que venía de Galaad un grupo de comerciantes ismaelitas. Sus camellos llevaban especias y resinas perfumadas para venderlas en Egipto.

fr.L: Et ils s’assirent pour manger du pain. Et ils levèrent les yeux et regardèrent, et voici, une caravane d’Ismaélites venait de Galaad, et leurs chameaux portaient de la gomme, du baume et de la myrrhe ; ils allaient [les] faire descendre en Égypte.
fr.B: Puis ils s’assirent pour prendre leur repas. Levant les yeux, ils virent une caravane d’Ismaélites qui venait de Galaad ; leurs chameaux étaient chargés de gomme, de baume et de résine, qu’ils emportaient en Égypte.
fr.R: Ensuite, les frères se sont assis pour manger. Ils ont levé les yeux et ils ont vu un groupe de marchands ismaélites qui venaient de Galaad. Leurs chameaux portaient des épices et des résines qui sentent bon, pour les vendre en Égypte.

sw.L: Nao wakaketi kula mkate. Nao wakainua macho yao wakatazama, na tazama, msafara wa Waishmaeli ulikuwa ukija kutoka Gileadi, na ngamia wao walikuwa wamebeba utomvu, zeri na manemane, wakisafiri kuvishusha mpaka Misri.
sw.B: Kisha wakaketi kula chakula. Walipoinua macho, waliona msafara wa Waishmaeli ukija kutoka Gileadi, ngamia wao wakiwa wamebeba utomvu wa miti, zeri na resini, wakivipeleka Misri.
sw.R: Kisha ndugu zake wakaketi kula. Walipotazama juu, waliona kundi la wafanyabiashara Waishmaeli wakija kutoka Gileadi. Ngamia wao walikuwa wamebeba viungo na utomvu wenye harufu nzuri, ili wakaviuze Misri.

decisions.choice: gum, balm and myrrh: costly plant resins
decisions.reason: These were aromatic resins, prized for perfume and medicine and shipped to Egypt, which used them widely, including in embalming. Gilead, east of the Jordan, was famous for its balm (Jeremiah 8:22). The exact plants are uncertain; lot was probably resin from the rockrose (cistus).

decisions.choice: they sat down to eat: callous indifference
decisions.reason: The brothers eat while Joseph is in the pit. Later they recall that they heard his cries for mercy and would not listen (42:21).

decisions.choice: a group of Ishmaelite traders
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a caravan was.

decisions.choice: "utomvu, zeri na manemane" (L); "utomvu wa miti, zeri na resini" (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no settled names for these three resins. "Utomvu" is plant gum or sap and "zeri" a soothing balm; Literal keeps "manemane" (myrrh) as the English Literal does, and Balanced says "resini", as the English Balanced says "resin", because the third resin (lot) was probably rockrose resin, not myrrh. "Ubani" would name frankincense, a different resin.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־אֶחָ֑יו מַה־בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י נַהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־אָחִ֔ינוּ וְכִסִּ֖ינוּ אֶת־דָּמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Judah to his brothers, what profit [is it] that we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

en.L: And Judah said to his brothers, "What profit [is it] if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?
en.B: Judah said to his brothers, "What do we gain by killing our brother and hiding the blood?
en.R: Judah said to his brothers, "What good will it do us if we kill our brother and hide what we did?

es.L: Y dijo Judá a sus hermanos: «¿Qué provecho [hay] en que matemos a nuestro hermano y encubramos su sangre?
es.B: Judá les dijo a sus hermanos: «¿Qué ganamos con matar a nuestro hermano y esconder la sangre?
es.R: Judá les dijo a sus hermanos: «¿De qué nos sirve matar a nuestro hermano y esconder lo que hicimos?

fr.L: Et Juda dit à ses frères : « Quel profit [y a-t-il] à tuer notre frère et à cacher son sang ?
fr.B: Juda dit à ses frères : « Que gagnerions-nous à tuer notre frère et à dissimuler son sang ?
fr.R: Juda a dit à ses frères : « À quoi cela nous servira-t-il de tuer notre frère et de cacher ce que nous avons fait ?

sw.L: Naye Yuda akawaambia ndugu zake, "Kuna faida gani tukimwua ndugu yetu na kuificha damu yake?
sw.B: Yuda akawaambia ndugu zake, "Tutapata nini kwa kumwua ndugu yetu na kuificha damu yake?
sw.R: Yuda akawaambia ndugu zake, "Tutafaidika nini tukimwua ndugu yetu na kuficha tulichofanya?

decisions.choice: conceal his blood: hide a murder
decisions.reason: Spilled blood was thought to cry out from the ground (4:10); covering it was an attempt to hide the crime (Job 16:18). Judah's argument is about profit, not mercy.

source.text: לְכ֞וּ וְנִמְכְּרֶ֣נּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים וְיָדֵ֨נוּ֙ אַל־תְּהִי־ב֔וֹ כִּֽי־אָחִ֥ינוּ בְשָׂרֵ֖נוּ ה֑וּא וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶחָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and our hand, let it not be on him, for our brother, our flesh [is] he. And listened his brothers.

en.L: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let not our hand be on him, for he [is] our brother, our own flesh." And his brothers listened.
en.B: Let us sell him to the Ishmaelites instead and keep our own hands off him. After all, he is our brother, our own flesh and blood." His brothers agreed.
en.R: Let us sell him to these Ishmaelites. Then we will not have to hurt him ourselves. After all, he is our brother and part of our own family." The other brothers agreed.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, vendámoslo a los ismaelitas, y no sea nuestra mano sobre él, porque él [es] nuestro hermano, nuestra carne». Y sus hermanos [lo] escucharon.
es.B: Mejor vendámoslo a los ismaelitas y no pongamos nuestras manos sobre él. Al fin y al cabo, es nuestro hermano, carne de nuestra carne». Sus hermanos estuvieron de acuerdo.
es.R: Vendámoslo a estos ismaelitas. Así no tendremos que hacerle daño nosotros mismos. Al fin y al cabo, es nuestro hermano y parte de nuestra propia familia». Los otros hermanos estuvieron de acuerdo.

fr.L: Venez, vendons-le aux Ismaélites, et que notre main ne soit pas sur lui, car il [est] notre frère, notre chair. » Et ses frères écoutèrent.
fr.B: Vendons-le plutôt aux Ismaélites, et ne portons pas la main sur lui. Après tout, c’est notre frère, notre chair et notre sang. » Ses frères y consentirent.
fr.R: Vendons-le à ces Ismaélites. Comme ça, nous n’aurons pas à lui faire de mal nous-mêmes. Après tout, c’est notre frère, il fait partie de notre famille. » Les autres frères ont été d’accord.

sw.L: Njooni, tumwuze kwa Waishmaeli, na mkono wetu usiwe juu yake, kwa maana yeye [ni] ndugu yetu, mwili wetu." Nao ndugu zake wakasikiliza.
sw.B: Afadhali tumwuze kwa Waishmaeli, tusimguse kwa mikono yetu. Hata hivyo, yeye ni ndugu yetu, ndugu yetu wa damu." Ndugu zake wakakubali.
sw.R: Tumwuze kwa hawa Waishmaeli. Hivyo hatutalazimika kumdhuru sisi wenyewe. Hata hivyo, yeye ni ndugu yetu, ni sehemu ya jamaa yetu." Ndugu wengine wakakubali.

decisions.choice: our flesh: our own close kin
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means family (29:14). Judah appeals to kinship while proposing to sell his brother as a slave.

source.text: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵף֙ מִן־הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And passed by men, Midianite[s], traders, and they drew and brought up Joseph from the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty [shekels of] silver; and they brought Joseph to Egypt.

en.L: And Midianite men, traders, passed by, and they drew up Joseph and lifted him out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty [shekels of] silver. And they took Joseph to Egypt.
en.B: When the Midianite traders came by, they pulled Joseph up out of the cistern and sold him to the Ishmaelites for {{units:about 8 ounces of silver|twenty shekels of silver}}, and they took Joseph away to Egypt.
en.R: When the Midianite traders came by, Joseph was pulled up out of the well and sold to the Ishmaelites for {{units:about 8 ounces of silver|twenty shekels of silver}}. Then the traders took Joseph to Egypt.

es.L: Y pasaron unos hombres madianitas, mercaderes, y tiraron de José y lo subieron del pozo, y vendieron a José a los ismaelitas por veinte [siclos de] plata. Y llevaron a José a Egipto.
es.B: Cuando pasaron los comerciantes madianitas, sacaron a José de la cisterna y lo vendieron a los ismaelitas por {{units:unos 230 gramos de plata|veinte siclos de plata}}, y se llevaron a José a Egipto.
es.R: Cuando pasaron los comerciantes madianitas, a José lo sacaron del pozo y lo vendieron a los ismaelitas por {{units:unos 230 gramos de plata|veinte siclos de plata}}. Luego los comerciantes se llevaron a José a Egipto.

fr.L: Et des hommes madianites, des marchands, passèrent, et ils tirèrent Joseph et le firent remonter de la fosse, et ils vendirent Joseph aux Ismaélites pour vingt [sicles d’]argent. Et ils emmenèrent Joseph en Égypte.
fr.B: Lorsque les marchands madianites passèrent, ils retirèrent Joseph de la citerne et le vendirent aux Ismaélites pour {{units:environ 230 grammes d’argent|vingt sicles d’argent}}, et ils emmenèrent Joseph en Égypte.
fr.R: Quand les marchands madianites sont passés, on a sorti Joseph du puits, et on l’a vendu aux Ismaélites pour {{units:environ 230 grammes d’argent|vingt sicles d’argent}}. Puis les marchands ont emmené Joseph en Égypte.

sw.L: Nao watu Wamidiani, wafanyabiashara, wakapita, wakamvuta, wakampandisha Yusufu kutoka shimoni, wakamwuza Yusufu kwa Waishmaeli kwa [shekeli] ishirini za fedha. Nao wakampeleka Yusufu Misri.
sw.B: Wafanyabiashara Wamidiani walipopita, walimvuta Yusufu kutoka katika shimo la maji, wakamwuza kwa Waishmaeli kwa {{units:karibu gramu 230 za fedha|shekeli ishirini za fedha}}, nao wakampeleka Yusufu Misri.
sw.R: Wafanyabiashara Wamidiani walipopita, Yusufu alitolewa kisimani, akauzwa kwa Waishmaeli kwa {{units:karibu gramu 230 za fedha|shekeli ishirini za fedha}}. Kisha wafanyabiashara hao wakampeleka Yusufu Misri.

decisions.choice: Midianites ... Ishmaelites: who pulled Joseph out and who sold him
alternatives: the Midianites pulled him out and sold him to the Ishmaelites, without the brothers
the brothers pulled him out and sold him to the Ishmaelites
decisions.reason: The subject of "drew" and "sold" is not stated. Read with verse 27, the brothers sell him; read on its own, the Midianites do it. "Ishmaelites" and "Midianites" may be overlapping names for the same desert traders (Judges 8:22-24 calls Midianites Ishmaelites), and Joseph himself later says to his brothers, "you sold me" (45:4). Reuben's surprise (verse 29) shows he was not there.

decisions.choice: twenty shekels of silver: the price of a young slave
decisions.reason: "Shekels" is understood. A shekel was a weight, about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams). Twenty shekels is the value set for a boy of five to twenty years in Leviticus 27:5.

decisions.choice: about 8 ounces of silver; with the Measures setting, twenty shekels of silver
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a modern weight by default and the original unit as the setting's alternative; Literal keeps the Hebrew "twenty [shekels of] silver".

decisions.choice: Joseph was pulled up ... and sold
alternatives: they pulled Joseph up ... and sold him
decisions.reason: Readable uses the passive to keep the Hebrew's unstated subject open.

decisions.choice: "a José lo sacaron del pozo y lo vendieron"
alternatives: "José fue sacado del pozo y vendido"
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject open with an impersonal third person plural, Joseph put first, rather than with the passive the English Readable uses, which sounds stiff in Spanish. Who did it stays unstated (m1).

decisions.choice: "on a sorti Joseph du puits, et on l'a vendu"
alternatives: "Joseph a été sorti du puits et vendu"
decisions.reason: Like the English Readable's passive, this leaves open who pulled Joseph out and sold him (m1). French says that with the impersonal "on", which reads more naturally than a passive of "sortir".

source.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל־הַבּ֔וֹר וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵין־יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבּ֑וֹר וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־בְּגָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And returned Reuben to the pit, and behold, not Joseph [was] in the pit; and he tore his clothes.

en.L: And Reuben returned to the pit, and look, Joseph [was] not in the pit; and he tore his clothes.
en.B: When Reuben came back to the cistern and saw that Joseph was gone, he tore his clothes in grief.
en.R: Later Reuben went back to the well, and Joseph was not there! Reuben tore his clothes because he was so upset.

es.L: Y volvió Rubén al pozo, y he aquí que José no [estaba] en el pozo; y rasgó sus vestidos.
es.B: Cuando Rubén volvió a la cisterna y vio que José ya no estaba, se rasgó la ropa en señal de dolor.
es.R: Más tarde Rubén regresó al pozo, ¡y José no estaba allí! Rubén se rasgó la ropa porque estaba muy angustiado.

fr.L: Et Ruben retourna à la fosse, et voici, Joseph n’[était] pas dans la fosse ; et il déchira ses vêtements.
fr.B: Quand Ruben revint à la citerne et vit que Joseph n’y était plus, il déchira ses vêtements de douleur.
fr.R: Plus tard, Ruben est retourné au puits, et Joseph n’était plus là ! Ruben a déchiré ses vêtements, tellement il était bouleversé.

sw.L: Naye Reubeni akarudi shimoni, na tazama, Yusufu hakuwamo shimoni; naye akararua nguo zake.
sw.B: Reubeni aliporudi kwenye shimo la maji na kuona kwamba Yusufu hayumo, alirarua nguo zake kwa huzuni.
sw.R: Baadaye Reubeni alirudi kisimani, na Yusufu hakuwepo! Reubeni akararua nguo zake kwa sababu alihuzunika sana.

decisions.choice: tore his clothes: a sign of grief and alarm
decisions.reason: Tearing one's garments was the customary gesture of mourning or distress (verse 34; 44:13).

decisions.choice: in grief / because he was so upset
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state what the gesture meant.

source.text: וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל־אֶחָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַיֶּ֣לֶד אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וַאֲנִ֖י אָ֥נָה אֲנִי־בָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned to his brothers and said, the boy, he is not; and I, where [am] I going?

en.L: And he returned to his brothers and said, "The boy is not [there]! And I, where shall I go?"
en.B: He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! And I, what am I going to do?"
en.R: He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! What am I going to do now?"

es.L: Y volvió a sus hermanos y dijo: «¡El muchacho no [está]! Y yo, ¿adónde iré?».
es.B: Volvió adonde estaban sus hermanos y les dijo: «¡El muchacho ha desaparecido! Y yo, ¿qué voy a hacer?».
es.R: Regresó adonde estaban sus hermanos y les dijo: «¡El muchacho no está! ¿Qué voy a hacer ahora?».

fr.L: Et il retourna vers ses frères et dit : « L’enfant n’[est] plus [là] ! Et moi, où irai-je ? »
fr.B: Il revint vers ses frères et leur dit : « Le garçon a disparu ! Et moi, que vais-je faire ? »
fr.R: Il est retourné vers ses frères et il leur a dit : « Le garçon a disparu ! Qu’est-ce que je vais faire maintenant ? »

sw.L: Naye akarudi kwa ndugu zake, akasema, "Kijana hayupo! Nami, niende wapi?"
sw.B: Akarudi kwa ndugu zake, akasema, "Kijana ametoweka! Na mimi, nitafanya nini?"
sw.R: Akarudi kwa ndugu zake, akasema, "Kijana hayupo! Nitafanya nini sasa?"

decisions.choice: where am I going?: what shall I do, how can I face my father?
decisions.reason: A cry of helplessness. As the firstborn, Reuben would have to answer to Jacob.

source.text: וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־כְּתֹ֣נֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took [the] tunic of Joseph, and they slaughtered a male goat of goats and dipped the tunic in the blood.

en.L: And they took Joseph's tunic and slaughtered a male goat and dipped the tunic in the blood.
en.B: They took Joseph's robe, killed a young goat, and soaked the robe in its blood.
en.R: Then the brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's robe in its blood.

es.L: Y tomaron la túnica de José, y degollaron un macho cabrío y mojaron la túnica en la sangre.
es.B: Tomaron la túnica de José, mataron un cabrito y empaparon la túnica en su sangre.
es.R: Luego los hermanos mataron un cabrito y mojaron la túnica de José en su sangre.

fr.L: Et ils prirent la tunique de Joseph, et ils égorgèrent un bouc et trempèrent la tunique dans le sang.
fr.B: Ils prirent la tunique de Joseph, tuèrent un jeune bouc et trempèrent la tunique dans son sang.
fr.R: Ensuite, les frères ont tué un chevreau et ils ont trempé la tunique de Joseph dans son sang.

sw.L: Nao wakaichukua kanzu ya Yusufu, wakachinja beberu wa mbuzi, wakaichovya kanzu katika damu.
sw.B: Wakaichukua kanzu ya Yusufu, wakachinja mwanambuzi, wakailowesha kanzu katika damu yake.
sw.R: Kisha ndugu zake wakachinja mbuzi, wakaichovya kanzu ya Yusufu katika damu yake.

decisions.choice: a goat: the deceiver deceived
decisions.reason: Jacob once deceived his own father using a young goat and his brother's clothes (27:9, 15-16). Now his sons deceive him with a goat and Joseph's robe. A young goat appears again in Judah's story (38:17).

source.text: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־כְּתֹ֣נֶת הַפַּסִּ֗ים וַיָּבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶל־אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר־נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם־לֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent [the] tunic of the palms and brought [it] to their father and said, this we have found; examine, please, [whether] the tunic of your son it [is], or not.

en.L: And they sent the tunic [reaching to the] wrists [and ankles], and they brought [it] to their father and said, "This we have found. Please examine [it, whether] it [is] your son's tunic or not."
en.B: They sent the long-sleeved robe to their father with the message, "We found this. Look it over and see whether it is your son's robe or not."
en.R: They sent the special robe to their father and said, "We found this. Look at it carefully. Does it belong to your son?"

es.L: Y enviaron la túnica [que llegaba hasta las] muñecas [y los tobillos], y [la] llevaron a su padre y dijeron: «Esto hemos encontrado. Examina, por favor, [si] es la túnica de tu hijo o no».
es.B: Enviaron la túnica larga con mangas a su padre con este mensaje: «Encontramos esto. Examínala y mira si es la túnica de tu hijo o no».
es.R: Le mandaron la túnica especial a su padre y le dijeron: «Encontramos esto. Míralo bien. ¿Es de tu hijo?».

fr.L: Et ils envoyèrent la tunique [qui descendait jusqu’aux] poignets [et aux chevilles], et ils [l’]apportèrent à leur père et dirent : « Nous avons trouvé ceci. Examine donc [si] c’[est] la tunique de ton fils ou non. »
fr.B: Ils firent porter la longue tunique à manches à leur père avec ce message : « Voici ce que nous avons trouvé. Regarde bien si c’est la tunique de ton fils ou non. »
fr.R: Ils ont envoyé la belle tunique à leur père et ils lui ont dit : « Nous avons trouvé ceci. Regarde-la bien. Est-ce qu’elle est à ton fils ? »

sw.L: Nao wakaipeleka kanzu [iliyofika hadi] vifundo [vya mikono na miguu], wakamletea baba yao, wakasema, "Hii tumeiona. Tafadhali ichunguze, [uone kama] ni kanzu ya mwanao au la."
sw.B: Waliipeleka ile kanzu ndefu yenye mikono mirefu kwa baba yao pamoja na ujumbe huu: "Tumeiokota hii. Ichunguze uone kama ni kanzu ya mwanao au la."
sw.R: Waliipeleka ile kanzu ya pekee kwa baba yao, wakasema, "Tumeiona hii. Iangalie vizuri. Je, ni ya mwanao?"

decisions.choice: examine, please (hakker-na): look closely and identify
decisions.reason: The same words return in 38:25, when Tamar asks Judah to identify his own seal and staff. Judah, who deceived his father with the words "examine, please", will be confronted with them.

source.text: וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he recognized it and said, [the] tunic of my son; an animal, wild, has eaten him; surely torn to pieces is Joseph.

en.L: And he recognized it and said, "[It is] my son's tunic! A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!"
en.B: He knew it at once. "It is my son's robe!" he cried. "Some wild animal has eaten him. Joseph has been torn apart, there is no doubt of it!"
en.R: Jacob knew the robe. He said, "It is my son's robe! A wild animal must have eaten him. Joseph has been torn to pieces!"

es.L: Y él la reconoció y dijo: «¡[Es] la túnica de mi hijo! Una fiera lo ha devorado. ¡Ciertamente José ha sido despedazado!».
es.B: La reconoció en el acto. «¡Es la túnica de mi hijo!», exclamó. «Alguna fiera lo ha devorado. ¡Sin duda José ha sido hecho pedazos!».
es.R: Jacob reconoció la túnica. Dijo: «¡Es la túnica de mi hijo! Un animal salvaje debe de habérselo comido. ¡A José lo han despedazado!».

fr.L: Et il la reconnut et dit : « [C’est] la tunique de mon fils ! Une bête sauvage l’a dévoré. Joseph a sûrement été mis en pièces ! »
fr.B: Il la reconnut aussitôt. « C’est la tunique de mon fils ! s’écria-t-il. Une bête féroce l’a dévoré. Joseph a été mis en pièces, il n’y a aucun doute ! »
fr.R: Jacob a reconnu la tunique. Il a dit : « C’est la tunique de mon fils ! Une bête sauvage a dû le manger. Joseph a été déchiré en morceaux ! »

sw.L: Naye akaitambua, akasema, "[Ni] kanzu ya mwanangu! Mnyama wa mwitu amemla. Hakika Yusufu ameraruliwa vipande vipande!"
sw.B: Akaitambua mara moja. Akapiga kelele, "Ni kanzu ya mwanangu! Mnyama mkali amemla. Bila shaka Yusufu amechanwa vipande vipande!"
sw.R: Yakobo aliitambua ile kanzu. Akasema, "Ni kanzu ya mwanangu! Lazima mnyama wa porini amemla. Yusufu ameraruliwa vipande vipande!"

decisions.choice: surely torn to pieces: the verb doubled in grief
decisions.reason: The doubled verb expresses certainty and anguish. Jacob reaches the conclusion his sons intended without their saying it (verse 20).

source.text: וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל־בְּנ֖וֹ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And tore Jacob his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.

en.L: And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his loins and mourned for his son many days.
en.B: Jacob tore his clothes, wrapped sackcloth around his waist, and grieved for his son a long time.
en.R: Jacob tore his clothes and put on rough cloth to show his sadness. He mourned for his son for a long time.

es.L: Y rasgó Jacob sus vestidos y puso tela de saco sobre sus lomos e hizo duelo por su hijo muchos días.
es.B: Jacob se rasgó la ropa, se ciñó la cintura con tela de saco e hizo duelo por su hijo durante mucho tiempo.
es.R: Jacob se rasgó la ropa y se puso ropa áspera para mostrar su tristeza. Lloró por su hijo durante mucho tiempo.

fr.L: Et Jacob déchira ses vêtements, et il mit un sac sur ses reins, et il prit le deuil de son fils pendant de nombreux jours.
fr.B: Jacob déchira ses vêtements, se ceignit les reins d’une toile de sac et porta longtemps le deuil de son fils.
fr.R: Jacob a déchiré ses vêtements et il a mis des habits de tissu grossier pour montrer sa tristesse. Il a pleuré son fils pendant longtemps.

sw.L: Naye Yakobo akararua nguo zake, akavaa gunia viunoni mwake, akaomboleza kwa ajili ya mwanawe siku nyingi.
sw.B: Yakobo alirarua nguo zake, akajifunga gunia kiunoni, akamwombolezea mwanawe kwa muda mrefu.
