sw.R: Yakobo alirarua nguo zake, akavaa nguo ya gunia kuonyesha huzuni yake. Akamlilia mwanawe kwa muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: sackcloth on his loins: rough goat-hair cloth worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth, coarse cloth usually of goat hair, was tied around the waist as a sign of grief or repentance.

decisions.choice: rough cloth to show his sadness
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom rather than naming the cloth.

source.text: וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל־בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל־בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּֽי־אֵרֵ֧ד אֶל־בְּנִ֛י אָבֵ֖ל שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ אֹת֖וֹ אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose all his sons and all his daughters to comfort him, and he refused to be comforted and said, for I will go down to my son mourning to Sheol. And wept for him his father.

en.L: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted and said, "No, I will go down to my son, mourning, to Sheol." Thus his father wept for him.
en.B: All his sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he would not be consoled. "No," he said, "I will go down to the grave still mourning for my son." And so his father wept for him.
en.R: All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but Jacob would not let them. He said, "I will still be sad for my son when I die and go to be with him in the grave." So Jacob kept crying for Joseph.

es.L: Y se levantaron todos sus hijos y todas sus hijas para consolarlo, pero él rehusó ser consolado y dijo: «No, descenderé hasta mi hijo, de luto, al Seol». Así lo lloró su padre.
es.B: Todos sus hijos y sus hijas fueron a consolarlo, pero él no quiso que lo consolaran. «No», dijo, «bajaré al lugar de los muertos todavía de luto por mi hijo». Y así su padre lo lloró.
es.R: Todos sus hijos y sus hijas trataron de consolarlo, pero Jacob no se dejó. Dijo: «Todavía estaré triste por mi hijo cuando me muera y vaya a estar con él en el lugar de los muertos». Así que Jacob siguió llorando por José.

fr.L: Et tous ses fils et toutes ses filles se levèrent pour le consoler, mais il refusa d’être consolé et dit : « Non, je descendrai vers mon fils, en deuil, au Shéol. » Ainsi son père le pleura.
fr.B: Tous ses fils et toutes ses filles vinrent le consoler, mais il ne voulut pas être consolé. « Non, dit-il, c’est en portant le deuil de mon fils que je descendrai au séjour des morts. » Et son père le pleura.
fr.R: Tous ses fils et toutes ses filles ont essayé de le consoler, mais Jacob n’a pas voulu. Il a dit : « Je serai encore triste pour mon fils quand je mourrai et que j’irai le rejoindre au séjour des morts. » Et Jacob a continué à pleurer Joseph.

sw.L: Nao wanawe wote na binti zake wote wakainuka ili kumfariji, lakini akakataa kufarijiwa, akasema, "Hapana, nitashuka kwa mwanangu, nikiomboleza, mpaka Kuzimu." Hivyo baba yake akamlilia.
sw.B: Wanawe wote na binti zake wote walikuja kumfariji, lakini hakukubali kufarijiwa. Akasema, "Hapana, nitashuka Kuzimu nikiwa bado ninamwombolezea mwanangu." Basi baba yake akamlilia.
sw.R: Wanawe wote na binti zake walijaribu kumfariji, lakini Yakobo hakukubali. Akasema, "Bado nitamhuzunikia mwanangu nitakapokufa na kwenda Kuzimu kuwa pamoja naye." Kwa hiyo Yakobo aliendelea kumlilia Yusufu.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place where all the dead go down, good and bad alike, pictured as deep beneath the earth. It is not a place of punishment in Genesis. Jacob means he will grieve until he dies (42:38; 44:29, 31).

decisions.choice: all his daughters: the women of the family
decisions.reason: Only one daughter, Dinah, has been named (30:21). "Daughters" may include daughters-in-law, or there may have been other daughters (46:7).

decisions.choice: his father: Jacob, rather than Isaac
decisions.reason: "His father" most naturally means Joseph's father, Jacob. Isaac's death is reported in 35:29, though the events may overlap in time.

decisions.choice: the grave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name Sheol; Balanced and Readable say "the grave", the plain sense here.

decisions.choice: "el lugar de los muertos" (B, R); "el Seol" (L)
decisions.reason: Spanish names the realm of the dead (m1) rather than "la tumba", a single burial place, as the Pentateuch's settled terms do; the sense is the same: Jacob will mourn until he dies.

decisions.choice: "le séjour des morts" (B, R); "le Shéol" (L)
decisions.reason: French uses the established term for Sheol, the realm of all the dead (m1), rather than "la tombe", a single burial place; Jacob's words mean he will mourn until he dies.

records.literal_gloss: And the Medanites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, [the] commander of the bodyguards.

en.L: And the Medanites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard.
en.B: Meanwhile the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the commander of his guard.
en.R: Meanwhile, in Egypt, the traders sold Joseph to Potiphar. Potiphar was one of Pharaoh's officials and the leader of the palace guard.

es.L: Y los medanitas lo vendieron en Egipto a Potifar, funcionario del faraón, jefe de la guardia.
es.B: Mientras tanto, los madianitas habían vendido a José en Egipto a Potifar, uno de los funcionarios del faraón, capitán de su guardia.
es.R: Mientras tanto, en Egipto, los comerciantes vendieron a José a Potifar. Potifar era uno de los funcionarios del faraón y el jefe de la guardia del palacio.

fr.L: Et les Médanites le vendirent en Égypte à Potiphar, officier de Pharaon, chef des gardes.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, les Madianites avaient vendu Joseph en Égypte à Potiphar, un des officiers de Pharaon, le chef de sa garde.
fr.R: Pendant ce temps, en Égypte, les marchands ont vendu Joseph à Potiphar. Potiphar était un des officiers de Pharaon et le chef des gardes du palais.

sw.L: Nao Wamedani wakamwuza huko Misri kwa Potifa, afisa wa Farao, mkuu wa walinzi.
sw.B: Wakati huo Wamidiani walikuwa wamemwuza Yusufu huko Misri kwa Potifa, mmoja wa maafisa wa Farao, mkuu wa walinzi wake.
sw.R: Wakati huo huko Misri, wale wafanyabiashara walimwuza Yusufu kwa Potifa. Potifa alikuwa mmoja wa maafisa wa Farao na mkuu wa walinzi wa jumba la mfalme.

decisions.choice: Medanites (the Hebrew text) or Midianites
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text spells the name Medanites here; the Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient translations have Midianites, as in verse 28. Medan and Midian were both sons of Abraham by Keturah (25:2), and the names may refer to the same group or be a variant spelling.

decisions.choice: an official (saris)
decisions.reason: Saris later came to mean a eunuch, but it is also a general title for a high royal officer, and Potiphar has a wife (39:7). Here it means an official.

decisions.choice: commander of the guard: literally "of the slaughterers"
decisions.reason: Tabbachim can mean butchers or cooks, but here it denotes the royal bodyguard, who also carried out executions; the commander had a prison in his house (40:3).

decisions.choice: the Midianites
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the spelling of verse 28 so the reader does not think a third group is meant; the footnote gives the Hebrew spelling.

decisions.choice: the traders
decisions.reason: Readable avoids a confusing new name.
